title: import module
goal: In this lesson you will learn the import statement, which loads a toolbox for your program to use.
learn: Write import math or import random
Know that the module name is ready to use afterwards
idea: You load a module with import math or import random, and you put imports near the top of the file. After that line runs, the module name is available. In the next lesson you will call its tools with a dot.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, add a third print that says Modules ready and press Run.

practice.text: Import math. Print a short message that math is ready.
practice.hint: Keep import math on top. On the next line, print() a short sentence that says math is ready.
practice.starterTip: Try: print("math is ready") right under import math.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if import math is present and a message prints.

practice.text: Import both math and random. Print ok.
practice.hint: Fill the two blank lines under the comment with import math and import random, one on each line.
practice.starterTip: Line 2: import math. Line 3: import random. The print("ok") at the bottom can stay as-is.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if both modules imported and ok prints.

quiz.question: Which line imports the math module?
quiz.correct: Right, import math loads that toolbox.

quiz.question: Where do imports usually go?

options.text: Near the top of the file

quiz.correct: Yes, the top of the file is the usual spot.

quiz.question: Does import run tools by itself?

options.text: No. It loads them for later use

quiz.correct: Right, import only loads the tools for later.
quiz.wrong: Loading is not the same as calling.

project.title: Load Two Toolboxes
project.desc: Import math and random. Print a labeled line for each saying it loaded. A short note is fine.
project.starter:
import math
import random
print()
print()
